title: Content `annotations`
description: The `audience`, `priority` and `lastModified` hints that content blocks, resources and prompt messages may carry.
question: Do content annotations survive to the agent?
notes: Annotations say who a block is for and how much it matters. No adapter that delivered the block delivered its annotations. LangChain is unmeasured here: its audio conversion raises on the same result, so the call aborts before this block can be observed. Isolating it needs a fixture that returns one block at a time.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI: every content block is dropped, annotations with them.
notes_by_num.2: OpenAI Agents: the text block survives; its annotations do not.
notes_by_num.3: Pydantic AI: the text block survives; its annotations do not.
notes_by_num.4: Mastra: every content block is dropped, annotations with them.

verdict.headline: Absent at every boundary where the block itself survived.
verdict.detail: audience and priority are the server's only way to say 'this part is for the model, this part is for the user'. Nothing downstream can recover them.

usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: Annotations are how a server says who a piece of content is for and how much it matters. A client that drops them cannot filter assistant-only content out of a user view, cannot prioritise what to keep when context runs short, and cannot sort by recency.
